ar: Add Windows Archive file support

Archives in ar format as written by Windows tools like lib.exe, separate
strings in string table directly with \0 instead of /\n.

GNU ar translates backslashes into slashes before the /\n check.

Handle both for improved compatibility, which also allows ar archives to
contain files in a directory structure.

An odd-sized table has its alignment byte outside the stored table.
Once the reader has consumed that byte, keep the last stored byte:
it is Windows payload and the consumed pad is the terminator. Until
then the historical NUL rewrite still applies. Remember an odd-sized
table in entry_offset and entry_padding so the caller can tell the
two cases apart.

Resolves #546

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

ar: Always skip all special entry bytes

The special file entries / and // are supposed to be properly padded,
but don't implicitly rely on it. Use archive_read_format_ar_skip
instead which takes care of possible padding bytes.

skip() clears the padding flag. For an odd-sized filename table,
record that the alignment byte was consumed so the string table
parser keeps a trailing Windows payload byte.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

ar: Improve error messages

Always use the term filename table and merge filename table size checks
into one.

When an odd-sized table's alignment byte is the terminator, put the
last stored byte back after parsing. That byte is Windows payload;
the parser's terminator rewrite must not keep it.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

coupling: GNU/Windows ar filename tables are malloc'd to the member size and must contain a NUL before archive_entry_copy_pathname -> strlen reads a long name. Three edits each preserve that NUL on their own and on well-formed tables (GNU '/\n' separators and Windows '\0' separators already terminate names), but any two of them drop it for an odd-sized table whose last byte is only an accepted pad ('\n', '`', or '\0') with no interior NUL. 109fcb2 stops rewriting the last byte when entry_offset and entry_padding are both set (the consumed alignment byte is treated as the terminator) and, on the way out, sets both fields for every odd table. At that commit nothing has set the fields yet, so the rewrite still runs and the new stores are cleared by the next header. 7d3a26b runs archive_read_format_ar_skip, which consumes the pad and clears entry_padding, then sets both fields again so the parser can see the pad was consumed. Without the parser exemption that record is ignored and the NUL is still written. 4da7708 saves the pre-parse last byte and restores it when those two fields are set after parsing, so a terminator rewrite does not clobber Windows payload. Without either of the other edits the fields stay clear and the saved byte is not restored. Together, 109fcb2+7d3a26b skip the rewrite, 109fcb2+4da7708 rewrite then put the pad byte back, and 7d3a26b+4da7708 do the same via the skip-path record. Reverting any one diff leaves one of those pairs, so the strlen over-read remains; each diff alone still plants a NUL inside the allocation. A repair has to keep a terminator that the allocation owns while still honouring all three rules (do not clobber payload once the pad is consumed, do remember that skip consumed it, and do restore the payload byte), which none of the diffs establishes by itself.
